confirmed: Source.version is correct: arXiv 2505.17241v1 [cs.HC], 22 May 2025, 22 pages; title and authors match p. 1. The entire markdown and all PDF pages, including references and final disclosures, were read.

Design and context are synthesis, with core=no: this paper searches and pools prior publications, with no original randomized people study (pp. 2-5, Sections 2.1-2.3). The participant threshold does not turn its pooled sample into an eligible experiment.

The paper reports 28 publications/studies, 127 effect-size estimates, and 8214 participants across included studies (pp. 1-3 and 14). It gives no original-trial randomized count; n_randomized=null is appropriate.
Search cutoff May 2, 2025; databases Web of Science, SSRN, arXiv; English publications from the past five years; one initial screener and two manually added studies (pp. 2-3, Section 2.1).

Hedges’ g is obtained from reported or converted Cohen’s d with a small-sample correction, pooled using a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model (p. 5, Section 2.3). The PDF does not specify a common participant-level standardizing SD; formulas are referred to the repository.

RQ2b without outlier study #4: g=-0.656, 95% CI [-0.913, -0.398]; Egger’s test and trim-and-fill were not run because of the number of studies (p. 14, Section 3.4.2). All values in the three reported strings and five synthesis.pooled entries match the PDF.

GPT-4 contributes 37 of 127 observations and GPT-3.5 contributes 25; creative writing 48, creative problem solving 25, alternate uses 12, and business-oriented ideation fewer than 15% (p. 8, Section 3.1). These are review-level frequencies.

Background counts reproduce p. 8: academia 85/127, laypeople 14, business 9. The source itself calls the remaining category 19 studies despite its effect-size-level framing; that wording is not independently verified as a count of distinct publications (Section 3 opening and Section 3.1).

Table 2 lists cosine similarity for CD01/CD02 and creativity scale for CD03/CD04, as the form notes; it also places Ismayilzada et al. [31] in both HAI11 and CD03 (p. 7). This confirms the review’s coding, not the underlying primary-study designs.

The one-line finding’s numbers and directions match pp. 8, 11 and 13. Matched follows the authors’ summary on p. 15; the statistical result is no significant difference. Table 3 rounds g to -0.05, 0.27 and -0.86 and has the caption/significance inconsistency already noted in the form.

The GitHub supplement is external to the PDF: database, conversion formulas, construct subgroup analyses, meta-regression, bias results, code and outputs are referenced on pp. 2-3, 5-6 and 22. The repository contents were not independently inspected.
No review protocol was preregistered, no external funding was received, and no competing interests were declared (p. 22, Review Protocol, Funding and Competing Interests).
summary: The arXiv v1 paper is correctly classified as a synthesis with no original randomized people study, and its reported counts and pooled statistics match the PDF. Four corrections concern AI modality, the spelling of Chai, a nonverbatim participant quote, and synthesis outcomes coded with an unsupported unit.
